newsitem.title: CHINA: China to import 2.6 million T edible oil in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to import 2.6 million T edible oil in 1997.

text.p: China's supply of edible oils is seen slightly exceeding demand this year, with imports to reach about 2.6 million tonnes in 1997, said an edition of the China Grains, Oils and Feeds newsletter seen in Beijing on Friday.
China would produce 6.7-6.8 million tonnes of edible oils in 1997 while stocks left over from last year stood at 1.0 million tonnes, the January 30 edition of the newsletter said.
The price of oilseeds would remain basically steady in 1997 and government intervention would help deal with any price fluctuations, the newsletter said.
Annual per capita consumption of edible oils would stay at around the 1996 level of 5.8 kg (12.8 lb), it said.

Area of land under oilseed crops had fallen by more than 134,000 hectares (330,000 acres) last year but output would be relatively good if ideal weather conditions persisted in southern growing areas, it said.
The growing area of cotton would likely continue to fall or hover around the 4.8 million hectares (11.9 million acres) of last year, it said.
Area under soybean was seen holding at last year's level, it said but gave no further details.
